$comment: The default locale, and therefore the key inventory: `npm run verify` fails the build
for a key present in a translation and absent here, because such a key renders
correctly in exactly one language and as a raw key everywhere else. Untranslated keys
in the other bundles are counted, not failed — fallback is per key, not per locale.
Nested for the benefit of translators; flattened to dotted keys once at load. A key
beginning with $ is a note like this one and never becomes a message.

app.name: Meridian
app.tagline: A CRM example application, built with the srl library

$nav-comment: nav.analytics and nav.billing are keyed by remote name: the shell asks for
nav.{name} for every remote in app.manifest.json, so mounting a remote needs one
message key and no code. nav.apps is the group they are listed under.
$breadcrumb-comment: The last step of a detail path when it is a word the route table chose rather
than an identifier out of the data. Only keywords belong here: an entry per
customer id would be a bundle the size of the database, and `shell-layout.js`
shows an unlisted segment as it stands for exactly that reason.

login.title: Sign in
login.lead: srl is the library; Meridian is the example CRM built with it. The session lives in an HttpOnly cookie set by the local server.
login.roleAdmin: every scope: sales writes, user administration, the audit log, and the analytics remote
login.roleOperator: sales writes and the analytics remote, but no user administration and no audit log
login.roleViewer: read only, and neither the analytics remote nor the administration screens

forbidden.title: Not allowed
forbidden.body: Your session does not carry the permission this area requires.
forbidden.signedInAs: Signed in as {name}. Signing in again will not change this.

dashboard.panelsLead: Each panel's module is fetched the first time it is selected. Choosing one swaps the outlet's child and re-renders nothing else on this screen.
dashboard.alertsLead: Products whose stock has fallen below their reorder point.
dashboard.alertsEmpty: Nothing is below its reorder point.

alert.belowReorder: {stock} in stock against a reorder point of {reorderPoint}.

orders.lead: Server-paginated: one page of rows and a total count per request, with paging, sorting and filtering done by the API.
orders.noCustomer: This order has no customer record.
orders.needsWriteScope: Advancing an order needs the sales:write scope.
orders.writeForbidden: The server refused: this session does not carry sales:write.
orders.historyEmpty: Nothing has happened to this order yet.

customers.lead: Client-paginated: forty-eight rows arrive once and the table filters, sorts and slices them locally.
customers.name: Customer
customers.needsWriteScope: Changing a customer needs the sales:write entitlement.

$customerForm-comment: The form's messages. Error codes come from the server as codes and are resolved here, so a validation failure is in the reader's language and follows a language change without a refetch.

customerForm.lead: Required fields are marked. Changes are saved when you submit.
customerForm.name: Company name
customerForm.contactsLimit: A customer may have at most {max} contacts.
customerForm.rejected: The server refused these values. See the fields below.
customerForm.discardPrompt: This form has changes that have not been saved.
customerForm.$error-comment: Only the codes this API invents. Everything the framework's own validators produce is standard collection text under ui.field.*, which is why this list is two entries rather than a dozen. duplicate is a rule about the set of contacts rather than about one of them, so no field validator could answer it.

error.duplicateContact: Another contact already uses this address.

products.lead: Infinite scrolling: each page is appended, and a filter or sort change starts the list again.
products.name: Product

movements.lead: The first page is a request; everything after it arrives on the event stream and is merged in front of it.

people.lead: The staff directory, filtered locally and paginated in the browser.
people.name: Name
people.hiredRecently: Hired in the last two years
people.hiredLongAgo: Hired more than five years ago

settings.name: Name
settings.subject: Subject

strategyNote.bff: The backend holds the tokens. This browser has an HttpOnly cookie it cannot read plus a CSRF token it can, so no credential appears anywhere in the application's JavaScript — which is why there is nothing to show above.
strategyNote.memory: The access token is in a module-scoped variable and dies with the tab. Nothing is in localStorage, and a strict CSP is what makes that worth anything.
strategyNote.dpop: Requests are signed by a non-extractable key. A stolen token is useless elsewhere, and script execution on this origin can still mint proofs.

settings.themeLead: The choice is stored as a UI preference like any other. `system` follows the operating system and re-renders when it changes.
settings.localeLead: One deployment for every language: switching re-renders every mounted component from a signal, with no reload and no per-locale bundle.
settings.storedStateLead: The sidebar's collapsed state, five tables' column layouts and three filters' values all cross one versioned, synchronous boundary. Nothing in the framework or the collection calls localStorage directly, which is why one screen can clear all of it.
settings.clearedTables: Cleared. The tables take their defaults on the next visit to each screen.
settings.clearedSidebar: Cleared. The sidebar starts expanded on the next load.
settings.usersLead: Accounts, not employees: an employee is a person in the HR system and a user is a login, administered by different people with different permissions.
settings.readOnlyNotice: This session can read accounts but not change them. The controls are shown disabled rather than hidden, because a control that vanishes is indistinguishable from a broken page.
settings.needsWriteScope: Changing an account needs the users:write scope.
settings.writeForbidden: The server refused: this session does not carry users:write.
settings.auditLead: Every mutating endpoint appends here, so the writes on the other screens are verifiable rather than merely present.

audit.$comment: Keyed by the action the server sends. An unknown action renders as itself rather than as a raw message key; see settings-audit.js.

$comment: Standard interaction text for the shared collection, resolved by
source/components/internal/text.js. The collection names these keys; this bundle owns
the language. An empty value is deliberate, not missing: `filter.from` and
`filter.to` emptied make a range chip read `3/3 – 3/7`.

dateRange.title: Pick a date range
dateRange.invalid: The end date is before the start date.

field.malformed: That is not a valid value.
field.notAllowed: That is not one of the allowed values.
field.future: That date is in the future.
field.past: That date is in the past.
